title: Prorate quota for partial KV-hit in composite (merged) requests
creator: Arjun Singh
description: Requests that are aggregated into composite batches currently get a single token/charge attribution per-request even when some inputs were served from the prefix/KV cache. This ticket standardizes prorated quota and rate-limit accounting for composite (merged) requests where only a subset of tokens were computed (cache hits) and the rest were generated by the model (cache misses). Goal: correct per-tenant billing and quota enforcement while preserving low-latency merged batching behaviour.
background: We observe two problematic behaviours: (1) Tenants pay full token charges when only a fraction of the request required model execution because prefix/KV cache returned most tokens; (2) Rate limiter and quota windows are triggered by merged-batch counts that do not reflect compute work (leading to inadvertent throttling). Existing tickets addressed related metering ambiguities (ENG-16421, ENG-24681) but did not implement a per-request prorating algorithm for composite batches or integrate it with the rate limiter. This ticket puts a concrete algorithm and end-to-end integration in place.
acceptance_criteria: Charge attribution is prorated per-request in merged batches: tokens served from cache are not billed at full compute token rate; charge rules documented and implemented.
Rate limiter counts treat partial-KV-hit requests as fractional compute units for quota and burst calculations; no tenant should be unfairly throttled due to high cache-hit volume.
End-to-end tests demonstrate correct billing on mixed scenarios: all-cache-hit, all-miss, and mixed where 10-90% tokens are cached.
Metric/monitoring dashboards added: per-tenant effective compute-tokens, cache-hit fraction, billed_tokens, and quota_consumption adjusted for prorating.
Migration plan for historical reconciliation documented (if required) and approved by Finance/RevOps.
implementation_notes: Define 'compute_token' as tokens generated by model runtime; 'cached_token' as tokens served from prefix/KV store. Use compute_token for billing unit; cached_token billed at reduced rate (configurable discount factor).

Add a fractional attribution field to aggregated-batch events: per_request {original_token_count, compute_token_count, cached_token_count}. Keep fields flat to avoid schema drift in metering pipeline.
Update metering pipeline step (ingest -> enrich -> aggregate) to sum compute_tokens rather than total_tokens for billing and quota enforcement. Preserve total_tokens for usage reporting.
Rate limiter: change token-bucket implementation to accept fractional tokens (float) and reservoir accounting per-tenant. Expose per-tenant burst capacity in dashboard.
Provide configuration: default cached_token discount = 0.05 compute-token-equivalent (5%), overridable per-customer via contract.
test_plan: Unit tests for prorate logic with edge cases: 0%, 1%, 50%, 99%, 100% cache-hit fractions.
Integration test that constructs merged batches with multiple tenants and validates billed amount and quota consumption per-tenant.
Load test on staging simulating bursty cached traffic to ensure rate limiter stability and no false throttles.
End-to-end reconciliation test comparing old and new metering outputs on sampled historical traces to validate delta and detect regressions.
Manual QA runbook for Finance to validate a small set of customer invoices before rollout.
deploy_plan: Feature flag behind 'prorated_metering_v1' for controlled rollout; default off in production until Finance sign-off.
Deploy metering pipeline change and rate-limiter change together in canary region, enable flag for internal tenants, run 48h smoke and reconciliation.
Gradually enable for customers with low billing volume, monitor billed_tokens delta and quota behaviour for 7 days before wider rollout.
Run revops migration script if reconciliation indicates >0.5% billing delta for a customer; otherwise record delta and proceed.
Rollback plan: flip feature flag off and revert rate-limiter behavior; keep compatibility layer to map fractional tokens back to integer buckets for legacy systems.
